learn.title: printf for files
learn.body: `fprintf(f, ...)` works like `printf`, but writes to the file `f`. To read, `fgets` fetches one line and `fscanf` reads formatted values. All three work on the `FILE *` you got from `fopen`.

learn.title: Writing lines
learn.body: This opens `scores.txt` for writing and puts two lines in it. Mode `"w"` creates the file or empties it.

learn.title: Reading lines
learn.body: This prints `got: ana 90` and `got: bo 85`. `fgets` reads up to the size you give it, including the newline, and returns `NULL` at the end of the file.

learn.title: Reading values
learn.body: `fscanf` returns how many values it filled. The loop stops when that is not 2. With the two lines above this prints 175. `%19s` limits the name to 19 letters, so it fits `name[20]`.

learn.title: Adding the scores
steps: The third finds the end and returns less than 2

learn.body: Never use `%s` in `fscanf` without a width. A long word would overflow your array, the same bug as a buffer overflow.
